cross_cutting_attack_questions.question: Are calibration blockers visible before numerical outputs are interpreted?
cross_cutting_attack_questions.required_evidence_or_review: Calibration-methods review, source-data plan, and blocker prominence review.
cross_cutting_attack_questions.what_would_fail: Any report path where placeholders are easier to see than the missing calibration basis.
cross_cutting_attack_questions.why_it_matters: Placeholder values can look precise even when no external calibration has occurred.

cross_cutting_attack_questions.question: Do ranges, bands, or matrices create false precision?
cross_cutting_attack_questions.required_evidence_or_review: Statistical, economic, and red-team review of band language.
cross_cutting_attack_questions.what_would_fail: Any phrasing that turns placeholder bands into empirical findings, forecasts, or confidence claims.
cross_cutting_attack_questions.why_it_matters: Deterministic bands and synthetic ranges are review aids only.

cross_cutting_attack_questions.question: Do manifests, reports, docs, runners, and CI steps refer to the same artefacts?
cross_cutting_attack_questions.required_evidence_or_review: Technical manifest trace and CI review.
cross_cutting_attack_questions.what_would_fail: Any missing report, untracked runner, stale document path, or CI ordering mismatch.
cross_cutting_attack_questions.why_it_matters: Stale manifests make the release package misleading even when models are unchanged.

cross_cutting_attack_questions.question: Could a reader overread this layer as more than a private prototype?
cross_cutting_attack_questions.required_evidence_or_review: Red-team language review and explicit non-claim retention.
cross_cutting_attack_questions.what_would_fail: Any wording that implies completed review, approval, validation, readiness, government endorsement, or legal adequacy.
cross_cutting_attack_questions.why_it_matters: The release materials are broad enough to be quoted without the surrounding caveats.

cross_cutting_attack_questions.question: Could evidence, workflow, or architecture language be mistaken for a real power or process?
cross_cutting_attack_questions.required_evidence_or_review: Legal, ATO-methods, administrative-law, and Parliamentary Counsel review.
cross_cutting_attack_questions.what_would_fail: Any path that reads like operative law, a statutory notice, enforcement step, penalty, or endorsed administrative process.
cross_cutting_attack_questions.why_it_matters: The prototype must not imply notices, penalties, powers, enforcement, or official administrative action.

cross_cutting_attack_questions.question: Does any path imply taxpayer-level, firm-level, industry, welfare, or government data was used?
cross_cutting_attack_questions.required_evidence_or_review: Repository guardrail review, secure-ingestion review, and privacy review.
cross_cutting_attack_questions.what_would_fail: Any committed artefact that looks like real evidence, restricted data, or government microdata.
cross_cutting_attack_questions.why_it_matters: The repository must remain synthetic-only and data-free.

core_attack_questions.question: Could a reader overread this layer as more than a private prototype?
core_attack_questions.required_evidence_or_review: Red-team language review and explicit non-claim retention.
core_attack_questions.what_would_fail: Any wording that implies completed review, approval, validation, readiness, government endorsement, or legal adequacy.
core_attack_questions.why_it_matters: The release materials are broad enough to be quoted without the surrounding caveats.

core_attack_questions.question: Are calibration blockers visible before numerical outputs are interpreted?
core_attack_questions.required_evidence_or_review: Calibration-methods review, source-data plan, and blocker prominence review.
core_attack_questions.what_would_fail: Any report path where placeholders are easier to see than the missing calibration basis.
core_attack_questions.why_it_matters: Placeholder values can look precise even when no external calibration has occurred.

core_attack_questions.question: Does any path imply taxpayer-level, firm-level, industry, welfare, or government data was used?
core_attack_questions.required_evidence_or_review: Repository guardrail review, secure-ingestion review, and privacy review.
core_attack_questions.what_would_fail: Any committed artefact that looks like real evidence, restricted data, or government microdata.
core_attack_questions.why_it_matters: The repository must remain synthetic-only and data-free.

core_attack_questions.question: Do ranges, bands, or matrices create false precision?
core_attack_questions.required_evidence_or_review: Statistical, economic, and red-team review of band language.
core_attack_questions.what_would_fail: Any phrasing that turns placeholder bands into empirical findings, forecasts, or confidence claims.
core_attack_questions.why_it_matters: Deterministic bands and synthetic ranges are review aids only.

core_attack_questions.question: Do manifests, reports, docs, runners, and CI steps refer to the same artefacts?
core_attack_questions.required_evidence_or_review: Technical manifest trace and CI review.
core_attack_questions.what_would_fail: Any missing report, untracked runner, stale document path, or CI ordering mismatch.
